hints: Focus on what cold, dilute manganate(VII) does to a C=C bond, it adds an OH group to each carbon of the double bond.
Draw out $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH=CH}_2$ and $\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CHCH}_3$ and add OH to the two alkene carbons in each case.
Classify each OH as primary, secondary or tertiary by counting carbons attached, and check which alkene can really show cis-trans isomerism.
walkthrough:
**Recall the diol reaction**

Cold, dilute acidified $\text{MnO}_4^-$ gives mild oxidation of an alkene to a diol. One OH adds to each carbon of the C=C bond.

$$\text{alkene + [O] + H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{diol (with 2 OH groups)}$$

**Draw the two diols**

For but-1-ene, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH=CH}_2$ becomes $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{OH}$. This is butane-1,2-diol.

For but-2-ene, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CHCH}_3$ becomes $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH(OH)CH}_3$. This is butane-2,3-diol.

**Classify the alcohol groups**

Remember, primary means the C-OH carbon is joined to 1 other carbon, secondary means joined to 2 other carbons.

In $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{OH}$, C1 is primary and C2 is secondary. In $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH(OH)CH}_3$, both C2 and C3 are secondary.

**Check cis-trans isomerism**

Cis-trans needs each C=C carbon to have two different groups. But-2-ene, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CHCH}_3$, can do this, but but-1-ene, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH=CH}_2$, cannot because one end has two identical H atoms.

So X and Y are correct, W and Z are incorrect.

options.A: W is wrong because neither diol has two primary OH groups. Butane-1,2-diol has one primary and one secondary, and butane-2,3-diol has two secondary. Y alone is correct here.
options.B: Both are wrong. W is wrong as no diol is primary-primary, and Z is wrong because only but-2-ene shows cis-trans isomerism, but-1-ene does not.
options.C: X is correct because but-1-ene gives $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{OH}$ with one primary and one secondary OH. Y is correct because but-2-ene gives $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH(OH)CH}_3$ with two secondary OH groups.
options.D: X is correct but Z is wrong. Students often think any butene shows cis-trans, but but-1-ene has $\text{=CH}_2$ with two H atoms on the same carbon, so cis-trans is impossible.
